parameters.content:
## The Alchemist
One sentence in. A checked n8n workflow out.

Type what you want automated. The Alchemist understands the goal, builds
a workflow, reviews or tests it depending on the type, and deploys it
directly to your n8n instance before handing it over.

**Main lane (top row):** handles intake, validation, the build loop, and
the final reply. Calls itself recursively via Run Section until done.

**Sections below:** eight independent sub-executions called by stage name:
- Understand (Sec 1): goal in, spec out
- Build (Sec 2): spec in, workflow JSON out
- Check (Sec 3): draft in, validated draft or errors out
- Review (Sec 4): blueprints only. LLM review pass with repair rounds
- Test (Sec 5): monitors only. Simulated mock checks & live smoke test
- Deploy (Sec 6): creates and optionally activates the workflow via n8n API
- Node Catalog (Sec 7): fetches core/AI node types and output schemas
- Test Mock (Sec 8): built-in webhook simulating HTTP responses for monitors

**Two output types:**
- Monitor: built, tested against the mock and live endpoint, auto-activated if an alert webhook is supplied.
- Blueprint: built, reviewed by a second LLM pass, handed over inactive for credential setup and activation. Best valid draft always delivered.

## Setup
1. Connect a Claude model to **Anthropic Model (Spec)** (Section 1),
   **Anthropic Model (Build)** (Section 2) and **Anthropic Model (Review)**
   (Section 4): your Anthropic API credential, or n8n's built-in AI credits
   on n8n Cloud. Default model: claude-sonnet-4-6.
2. Add your n8n API credential to **Create Workflow** and **Activate
   Workflow** in Section 6: Deploy. Base URL: your instance URL + /api/v1.
3. The chat is public by default: anyone with the link can use it. To limit
   it, open **Chat Trigger** and set Authentication to Basic Auth (a user
   name and a password).
4. Open **Settings**. Leave PUBLIC_URL empty to detect your instance URL
   automatically, or set it (e.g. https://myinstance.app.n8n.cloud) when
   n8n runs behind a proxy. The other values:
   - CORE_NODES_VERSION / AI_NODES_VERSION: the node catalog is pinned
     to n8n-nodes-base 2.39.7 and @n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain 2.39.8. To
     upgrade, change both together, then re-test before publishing.
   - MAX_ATTEMPTS: build and repair rounds (1 to 5).
   - TIME_BUDGET_MINUTES: no new repair round after this time.
   - PENDING_QUESTION_MINUTES: how long an open question waits for an answer.
   - DAILY_RUNS_PER_CHAT / DAILY_RUNS_TOTAL: builds per day (0 = no limit).
     Soft limits: two chats at the same moment can let one extra run through.
5. In this workflow's settings, set Timeout Workflow to 20 minutes. It must
   be longer than TIME_BUDGET_MINUTES, so the build loop stops in time to
   send a reply.
6. Save and **Publish** this workflow. Sections call the published version
   via Execute Workflow. Publish after every edit or the sections run stale.
7. Open **Chat Trigger**, copy the public chat URL, and open it in your
   browser or share it with users.
8. Optional: a run that hits the timeout ends without a chat reply. To get
   notified, set an error workflow in this workflow's settings.

## Section router
Run Section calls this workflow with a stage field set to understand,
build, check, review, test, deploy, or catalog. Section Trigger receives the
call and Route to Section routes by index position.
An unknown stage goes to Unknown Stage, which returns an error reply.

Monitors follow: Understand > Build > Check > Test > Deploy.
Blueprints follow: Understand > Build > Check > Review > Deploy.
For blueprints, Build calls Catalog (Section 7) for the node catalogue, and
Check calls it for the output schemas.

Each section receives the full state object, does its work, and returns
a result to Decide Next Step in the main lane. End Understand and End
Build exist because an LLM can fail at those points: they put the state
back on the item so Decide Next Step can handle the failure cleanly.
Check ends in End Check, Review in Finish Blueprint (handles both success
and failed review), Test in Score Tests, Deploy in Write Verdict or Report
Deploy Error.

Welcome to The Alchemist.
Tell me what you want automated in one sentence. I'll build it and check it as hard as I can before handing it to you.
Try: Alert me on any GitHub incident

parameters.content:
## Section 1: Understand
**Goal in, spec out.**

- Probes user-provided URLs; drops unsupported checks or halts on bad redirects/errors.
- LLM maps the goal to a structured JSON spec (monitor or blueprint).
- Blocks prompt injections, local IPs, and non-automation tasks.
- Retries on malformed output; gracefully halts if the AI model is overloaded.

## Section 2: Build
**Spec in, workflow JSON out.**

- Blueprints fetch pinned n8n and AI node catalogs (Section 7) to ensure valid node generation.
- Injects exact error feedback from prior attempts during repair loops.
- Parses the LLM's JSON and extracts a slimmed-down catalog for the Check phase.

// Builds the prompt for the Build step.
// - Monitors get the strict monitor contract. A validator and a hidden test harness check every rule.
// - Blueprints get general rules. What each node needs comes from the node catalog added below the task.
// On a retry, the prompt also includes the workflow to repair and what went wrong.

const MONITOR_INSTRUCTIONS = [
  "You generate n8n workflows as JSON. The workflow is an HTTP health monitor that implements a given SPEC exactly.",
  "",
  "OUTPUT SHAPE:",
  "{\"name\": string, \"nodes\": [{\"name\": string, \"type\": string, \"typeVersion\": number, \"position\": [x, y], \"parameters\": {}, \"onError\": optional string}], \"connections\": {\"<source node name>\": {\"main\": [[{\"node\": \"<target node name>\", \"type\": \"main\", \"index\": 0}]]}}}",
  "Do not include ids, settings or credentials. Space nodes 220px apart on x.",
  "",
  "HARD CONTRACT (a validator and a hidden test harness enforce every rule):",
  "1. Two triggers: a node named \"Schedule\" (scheduleTrigger) and a node named \"Test Entry\" (executeWorkflowTrigger with parameters {\"inputSource\": \"passthrough\"}). Both connect to \"Config\".",
  "2. \"Config\" is a Set node with exactly these three fields and production defaults:",
  "   targetUrl (string) = {{ $json.targetUrl ?? '<the spec targetUrl, exactly>' }}",
  "   alertWebhookUrl (string) = {{ $json.alertWebhookUrl ?? '<given alert webhook, or https://hooks.slack.com/services/REPLACE_ME>' }}",
  "   timeoutMs (number) = {{ $json.timeoutMs ?? 10000 }}",
  "   Every later node reads these through $('Config').item.json.<field>. Never hardcode them elsewhere.",
  "3. Implement the status check plus EVERY check in the spec. A run is UNHEALTHY when, in this priority order:",
  "   a. the GET failed (its output has an \"error\" field: timeout, DNS, connection),",
  "   b. the status is not 2xx. Exception: if the spec has a rateLimit check and the status is 429, the run is HEALTHY with a reason containing 'rate limited',",
  "   c. any spec check fails.",
  "4. On UNHEALTHY: HTTP POST to alertWebhookUrl with JSON body {\"text\": \"<service>: <cause>\"}. The text starts with the service name. The POST node MUST have \"onError\": \"continueRegularOutput\".",
  "5. Every run ends in exactly one of two Set nodes:",
  "   \"Result OK\": alert (boolean, false) and reason (string, e.g. 'HTTP 200').",
  "   \"Result Alert\": alert (boolean, true) and reason (string), placed AFTER the POST. Reason = the cause, plus ' (alert delivery failed)' when the POST output has an \"error\" field.",
  "   A reason is NEVER empty.",
  "6. Maximum 20 nodes. Only the node types listed below.",
  "7. ONE VISIBLE NODE PER CHECK. The canvas must show the logic: every check is its own IF node, chained on the true branch:",
  "   \"Reachable?\" (!$json.error) -> \"Status 2xx?\" -> one IF per spec check -> \"Result OK\".",
  "   Every false branch goes to its own Set node named \"Cause: <what failed>\" with one field, cause (string).",
  "   All \"Cause: ...\" nodes connect to ONE noOp node named \"Unhealthy\", then \"Send Alert\", then \"Result Alert\".",
  "   IF nodes pass their input through unchanged, so inside the chain $json is still the GET output.",
  "   After \"Unhealthy\", read the cause with $('Unhealthy').item.json.cause.",
  "8. JSON safety: inside n8n expressions, write string literals with single quotes ('like this'), never double quotes. No comments, no trailing commas.",
  "",
  "READING THE GET OUTPUT: fullResponse is on, so the output has statusCode, headers and the body. The body is $json.body when the response is JSON (already parsed into an object) and $json.data when it is text.",
  "An \"error\" field may be a string or an object with \"message\": use String($json.error?.message || JSON.stringify($json.error)).",
  "DATA FLOW: a Set node outputs ONLY the fields it sets. After any Set node, $json no longer has statusCode, body, data or error.",
  "Read the GET result anywhere after that with $('<GET node name>').item.json.statusCode (and .body, .data, .error).",
  "",
  "HOW TO IMPLEMENT EACH CHECK TYPE:",
  "- jsonField {path, equals}: read the field from the parsed body with optional chaining, e.g. $json.body?.status?.indicator. Fails when missing or different. Cause: '<path> is <actual value> (expected <equals>)', and '<path> is missing (expected <equals>)' when the field does not exist. Never print 'undefined'.",
  "- keyword {text}: search a string version of the body: (typeof ($json.body ?? $json.data) === 'string' ? ($json.body ?? $json.data) : JSON.stringify($json.body ?? $json.data ?? '')). Fails when the text is absent. Cause: 'keyword <text> not found'.",
  "- latency {maxMs}: add a Set node named \"Start Timer\" between Config and the GET, with field startedAt (number) = {{ $now.toMillis() }}. After the GET: elapsedMs = $now.toMillis() - $('Start Timer').item.json.startedAt. Fails when elapsedMs > maxMs. Cause: 'slow response: <elapsedMs> ms (limit <maxMs> ms)'.",
  "- rateLimit: see rule 3b.",
  "NODE NAMES per check (use these): jsonField -> IF \"<Field> OK?\" (e.g. \"Indicator OK?\") + Set \"Cause: Wrong <Field>\".",
  "keyword -> IF \"Keyword Found?\" + Set \"Cause: Keyword Missing\". latency -> Set \"Start Timer\" before the GET, IF \"Fast Enough?\" + Set \"Cause: Slow Response\".",
  "rateLimit -> IF \"Rate Limited?\" placed BEFORE \"Status 2xx?\" on the true branch of \"Reachable?\": its true branch goes to \"Result OK\", its false branch continues to \"Status 2xx?\".",
  "",
  "ALLOWED NODES (type @ typeVersion, then a parameter template):",
  "",
  "n8n-nodes-base.scheduleTrigger @ 1.2",
  "{\"rule\": {\"interval\": [{\"field\": \"minutes\", \"minutesInterval\": 5}]}}",
  "",
  "n8n-nodes-base.executeWorkflowTrigger @ 1.1",
  "{\"inputSource\": \"passthrough\"}",
  "",
  "n8n-nodes-base.set @ 3.4",
  "{\"assignments\": {\"assignments\": [{\"id\": \"a1\", \"name\": \"fieldName\", \"type\": \"string\", \"value\": \"={{ expression }}\"}]}, \"options\": {}}",
  "Allowed assignment types: string, number, boolean.",
  "",
  "n8n-nodes-base.httpRequest @ 4.2",
  "GET: {\"method\": \"GET\", \"url\": \"={{ $('Config').item.json.targetUrl }}\", \"options\": {\"timeout\": \"={{ $('Config').item.json.timeoutMs }}\", \"response\": {\"response\": {\"fullResponse\": true, \"neverError\": true}}}}",
  "POST: {\"method\": \"POST\", \"url\": \"={{ $('Config').item.json.alertWebhookUrl }}\", \"sendBody\": true, \"specifyBody\": \"json\", \"jsonBody\": \"={{ JSON.stringify({ text: '<service>: ' + $('Unhealthy').item.json.cause }) }}\", \"options\": {}}",
  "neverError stops non-2xx statuses from throwing; timeouts and connection errors still throw.",
  "Node-level option \"onError\": \"continueRegularOutput\" turns a thrown error into an output item with an \"error\" field.",
  "",
  "n8n-nodes-base.if @ 2.2",
  "{\"conditions\": {\"options\": {\"caseSensitive\": true, \"leftValue\": \"\", \"typeValidation\": \"loose\", \"version\": 2}, \"conditions\": [{\"id\": \"c1\", \"leftValue\": \"={{ boolean expression }}\", \"rightValue\": \"\", \"operator\": {\"type\": \"boolean\", \"operation\": \"true\", \"singleValue\": true}}], \"combinator\": \"and\"}, \"options\": {}}",
  "Output index 0 is the true branch, index 1 is the false branch.",
  "",
  "n8n-nodes-base.noOp @ 1",
  "{}",
  "",
  "BASELINE EXAMPLE: a correct workflow for a spec with NO extra checks (status only), for a different service. Reuse its triggers, Config, IF chain and alert pattern. For every check in your spec, ADD its IF node and its Cause node into the chain, and name your service in the alert text.",
  "{\"name\": \"Example.com Health Monitor\", \"nodes\": [{\"name\": \"Schedule\", \"type\": \"n8n-nodes-base.scheduleTrigger\", \"typeVersion\": 1.2, \"position\": [0, 0], \"parameters\": {\"rule\": {\"interval\": [{\"field\": \"minutes\", \"minutesInterval\": 5}]}}}, {\"name\": \"Test Entry\", \"type\": \"n8n-nodes-base.executeWorkflowTrigger\", \"typeVersion\": 1.1, \"position\": [0, 200], \"parameters\": {\"inputSource\": \"passthrough\"}}, {\"name\": \"Config\", \"type\": \"n8n-nodes-base.set\", \"typeVersion\": 3.4, \"position\": [220, 100], \"parameters\": {\"assignments\": {\"assignments\": [{\"id\": \"con0\", \"name\": \"targetUrl\", \"type\": \"string\", \"value\": \"={{ $json.targetUrl ?? 'https://example.com/health' }}\"}, {\"id\": \"con1\", \"name\": \"alertWebhookUrl\", \"type\": \"string\", \"value\": \"={{ $json.alertWebhookUrl ?? 'https://hooks.slack.com/services/REPLACE_ME' }}\"}, {\"id\": \"con2\", \"name\": \"timeoutMs\", \"type\": \"number\", \"value\": \"={{ $json.timeoutMs ?? 10000 }}\"}]}, \"options\": {}}}, {\"name\": \"Check Endpoint\", \"type\": \"n8n-nodes-base.httpRequest\", \"typeVersion\": 4.2, \"position\": [440, 100], \"onError\": \"continueRegularOutput\", \"parameters\": {\"method\": \"GET\", \"url\": \"={{ $('Config').item.json.targetUrl }}\", \"options\": {\"timeout\": \"={{ $('Config').item.json.timeoutMs }}\", \"response\": {\"response\": {\"fullResponse\": true, \"neverError\": true}}}}}, {\"name\": \"Reachable?\", \"type\": \"n8n-nodes-base.if\", \"typeVersion\": 2.2, \"position\": [660, 100], \"parameters\": {\"conditions\": {\"options\": {\"caseSensitive\": true, \"leftValue\": \"\", \"typeValidation\": \"loose\", \"version\": 2}, \"conditions\": [{\"id\": \"c1\", \"leftValue\": \"={{ !$json.error }}\", \"rightValue\": \"\", \"operator\": {\"type\": \"boolean\", \"operation\": \"true\", \"singleValue\": true}}], \"combinator\": \"and\"}, \"options\": {}}}, {\"name\": \"Status 2xx?\", \"type\": \"n8n-nodes-base.if\", \"typeVersion\": 2.2, \"position\": [880, 0], \"parameters\": {\"conditions\": {\"options\": {\"caseSensitive\": true, \"leftValue\": \"\", \"typeValidation\": \"loose\", \"version\": 2}, \"conditions\": [{\"id\": \"c1\", \"leftValue\": \"={{ $json.statusCode >= 200 && $json.statusCode < 300 }}\", \"rightValue\": \"\", \"operator\": {\"type\": \"boolean\", \"operation\": \"true\", \"singleValue\": true}}], \"combinator\": \"and\"}, \"options\": {}}}, {\"name\": \"Result OK\", \"type\": \"n8n-nodes-base.set\", \"typeVersion\": 3.4, \"position\": [1100, -100], \"parameters\": {\"assignments\": {\"assignments\": [{\"id\": \"res0\", \"name\": \"alert\", \"type\": \"boolean\", \"value\": \"={{ false }}\"}, {\"id\": \"res1\", \"name\": \"reason\", \"type\": \"string\", \"value\": \"={{ 'HTTP ' + $json.statusCode }}\"}]}, \"options\": {}}}, {\"name\": \"Cause: Connection Error\", \"type\": \"n8n-nodes-base.set\", \"typeVersion\": 3.4, \"position\": [880, 300], \"parameters\": {\"assignments\": {\"assignments\": [{\"id\": \"cau0\", \"name\": \"cause\", \"type\": \"string\", \"value\": \"={{ 'connection error: ' + String($json.error?.message || JSON.stringify($json.error)).slice(0, 200) }}\"}]}, \"options\": {}}}, {\"name\": \"Cause: Bad Status\", \"type\": \"n8n-nodes-base.set\", \"typeVersion\": 3.4, \"position\": [1100, 100], \"parameters\": {\"assignments\": {\"assignments\": [{\"id\": \"cau0\", \"name\": \"cause\", \"type\": \"string\", \"value\": \"={{ 'HTTP ' + $json.statusCode + ' from ' + $('Config').item.json.targetUrl }}\"}]}, \"options\": {}}}, {\"name\": \"Unhealthy\", \"type\": \"n8n-nodes-base.noOp\", \"typeVersion\": 1, \"position\": [1320, 200], \"parameters\": {}}, {\"name\": \"Send Alert\", \"type\": \"n8n-nodes-base.httpRequest\", \"typeVersion\": 4.2, \"position\": [1540, 200], \"onError\": \"continueRegularOutput\", \"parameters\": {\"method\": \"POST\", \"url\": \"={{ $('Config').item.json.alertWebhookUrl }}\", \"sendBody\": true, \"specifyBody\": \"json\", \"jsonBody\": \"={{ JSON.stringify({ text: 'Example: ' + $('Unhealthy').item.json.cause }) }}\", \"options\": {}}}, {\"name\": \"Result Alert\", \"type\": \"n8n-nodes-base.set\", \"typeVersion\": 3.4, \"position\": [1760, 200], \"parameters\": {\"assignments\": {\"assignments\": [{\"id\": \"res0\", \"name\": \"alert\", \"type\": \"boolean\", \"value\": \"={{ true }}\"}, {\"id\": \"res1\", \"name\": \"reason\", \"type\": \"string\", \"value\": \"={{ $('Unhealthy').item.json.cause + ($json.error ? ' (alert delivery failed)' : '') }}\"}]}, \"options\": {}}}], \"connections\": {\"Schedule\": {\"main\": [[{\"node\": \"Config\", \"type\": \"main\", \"index\": 0}]]}, \"Test Entry\": {\"main\": [[{\"node\": \"Config\", \"type\": \"main\", \"index\": 0}]]}, \"Config\": {\"main\": [[{\"node\": \"Check Endpoint\", \"type\": \"main\", \"index\": 0}]]}, \"Check Endpoint\": {\"main\": [[{\"node\": \"Reachable?\", \"type\": \"main\", \"index\": 0}]]}, \"Reachable?\": {\"main\": [[{\"node\": \"Status 2xx?\", \"type\": \"main\", \"index\": 0}], [{\"node\": \"Cause: Connection Error\", \"type\": \"main\", \"index\": 0}]]}, \"Status 2xx?\": {\"main\": [[{\"node\": \"Result OK\", \"type\": \"main\", \"index\": 0}], [{\"node\": \"Cause: Bad Status\", \"type\": \"main\", \"index\": 0}]]}, \"Cause: Connection Error\": {\"main\": [[{\"node\": \"Unhealthy\", \"type\": \"main\", \"index\": 0}]]}, \"Cause: Bad Status\": {\"main\": [[{\"node\": \"Unhealthy\", \"type\": \"main\", \"index\": 0}]]}, \"Unhealthy\": {\"main\": [[{\"node\": \"Send Alert\", \"type\": \"main\", \"index\": 0}]]}, \"Send Alert\": {\"main\": [[{\"node\": \"Result Alert\", \"type\": \"main\", \"index\": 0}]]}}}"
].join('\n');

// Only general rules and neutral templates here. What a given node or service needs comes from the
// node catalog added below the task (fields, versions, resources, format rules from n8n's own help text).
// KEEP IN SYNC: the "NEVER use" list in rule 2 must match BLOCKED_TYPES in "Validate Blueprint Draft".
const BLUEPRINT_INSTRUCTIONS = [
  "You generate an n8n workflow as JSON: a clean STARTING POINT the user will open, connect accounts to, and finish. It is imported, not executed.",
  "",
  "OUTPUT SHAPE:",
  "{\"name\": string, \"nodes\": [{\"name\": string, \"type\": string, \"typeVersion\": number, \"position\": [x, y], \"parameters\": {}}], \"connections\": {\"<source node name>\": {\"main\": [[{\"node\": \"<target node name>\", \"type\": \"main\", \"index\": 0}]]}}}",
  "Do not include ids, settings or credentials. Positions are recalculated automatically.",
  "",
  "RULES:",
  "GENERAL:",
  "1. Use the node types, typeVersions (the newest listed), resources, operations and field names from the NODES FOR THIS GOAL catalogue below, exactly. A field listed \"when resource=... operation=...\" only exists there. NATIVE NODES FIRST: when a service has its own node, use it, never an HTTP Request to its API.",
  "2. NEVER use: code, aiTransform (AI Transform), function, functionItem, executeCommand, ssh, ftp, git, n8n (API), readWriteFile, readBinaryFile(s), writeBinaryFile, localFileTrigger, executeWorkflow, or the LangChain Code Tool, Call n8n Workflow Tool, Workflow Retriever and Tool Executor. Use Set and IF expressions instead of code.",
  "3. Never include credentials. Nodes that need an account simply have none; the user connects them later.",
  "4. Exactly one trigger node. Name every node by what it does.",
  "5. Expressions use {{ }}; inside them use single quotes for strings.",
  "6. DATA FROM EARLIER NODES: $json only reads the node DIRECTLY before. For anything earlier use $('Exact Node Name').item.json.<field>, and that node must come BEFORE on a connection path (not on a side branch). Never use the old $node[\"Name\"] syntax.",
  "7. REQUIRED FIELDS: every field the catalogue marks as required must be set, in the shape it shows (resource locators as {\"__rl\": true, \"mode\": \"list\", \"value\": \"...\"}).",
  "8. COMPLETE CONFIGURATION: fill every field the step needs with a real value or an expression from earlier data. Never leave a mapping, a message body or a set of fields empty.",
  "DATA FLOW:",
  "9. ONE ITEM = ONE OBJECT: n8n runs every node once per item. Never index items like .item.json[0]. A list operation already returns one full record per item: do not add a per-item \"get\" of the same record. If the node has a \"simple\" / \"simplify\" option that trims the record and you need the full data (a full message body), set it to false.",
  "10. NEW RECORDS ONLY: a schedule that reads a list gets the SAME records again on every run. When the service has a trigger node for new records (its name ends in Trigger), use it instead of schedule + list. Otherwise put Remove Duplicates (template below) right after the read, or mark each record as processed at the END of the chain (after the last step, not on a side branch). If the read node has a time filter (received after, updated since...), set it to twice the schedule interval, e.g. ={{ $now.minus({ minutes: 30 }).toISO() }} for every 15 minutes. A daily digest that aggregates the list is fine as it is.",
  "11. DIGESTS AND SUMMARIES: a send node runs once PER ITEM. When the goal wants ONE digest, summary or report of many items, put an Aggregate node before the send node and join the list in the message.",
  "12. CLOCK TIMES: when the goal names a time (\"at 8 AM\", \"every morning at 08:00\"), use a daily schedule with triggerAtHour, never \"every 24 hours\".",
  "13. MESSAGE FORMAT: a node with a body-format option (text / html / markdown) must match the content: markdown or plain text is \"text\"; HTML needs real HTML or a Markdown node (markdownToHtml) first.",
  "14. READ ONLY FIELDS A NODE REALLY OUTPUTS. A webhook's caller data is under .body; never pass a whole trigger item on (it can contain request headers). Chat apps limit message length: cut long LLM replies with .slice(0, 4000) before sending them to a chat. A webhook that answers its caller (Respond to Webhook) replies as soon as the data is saved, before optional notifications (Slack, email), so a slow or failing notification does not break the reply. An HTTP Request whose answer is a top-level JSON array outputs one item per element: there is no .data field to split out.",
  "AI STEPS:",
  "15. To summarise, classify or rewrite with an LLM use @n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain.chainLlm with a chat model node attached via ai_languageModel (template below); read the reply as $('<chain name>').item.json.text. To EXTRACT several fields use @n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain.informationExtractor with one attribute per field; each field is $('<extractor name>').item.json.output.<attribute>. Use the chat model node the request names (Anthropic, Gemini, Ollama...), OpenAI's when none is named. NEVER JSON.parse an LLM reply. A model the request names (Claude, GPT, Gemini) is a chat model sub-node (lmChatAnthropic, lmChatOpenAi, ...) attached to a Text Classifier, chain or agent. Use the Anthropic or OpenAI app node only for images, audio, files or assistants.",
  "16. LLM PROMPTS: Basic LLM Chain and AI Agent ALWAYS need \"promptType\": \"define\" with the prompt in \"text\", unless the trigger is a Chat Trigger. Without it they ignore \"text\".",
  "17. CATEGORIES: to ROUTE items by category (a different action per category), use @n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain.textClassifier (template below): one category per output, a chat model attached via ai_languageModel, and every category output the request needs connected, or items of the other categories are dropped. Only when the category must be STORED or shown (a field, a column, a label in a message), make the LLM answer with exactly one of fixed values in its own field: best an Information Extractor attribute whose description says \"Exactly one of: A, B, C\" (it is turned into a strict list of allowed values).",
  "18. FORMS PEOPLE FILL IN: every field the request lists is required. A fixed set of choices or a rating (1 to 5) is a dropdown with its options; long free text is a textarea; an email address is an email field.",
  "19. RECORDS AND MAPPINGS: every row of a field mapping (properties, fields, columns) sets a VALUE from the data, not only the key or column name, in the key format the catalogue states. When the request says a database, table or sheet, ADD A RECORD to it (the resource and operation that create a row or database item), not a page or a document.",
  "ACCOUNTS:",
  "20. ACCOUNT IDS YOU CANNOT KNOW (list, sheet, channel, database, board IDs...): when the request names one (\"#hiring\", an email address, a sheet name), USE IT exactly. Otherwise leave it empty: \"\" or {\"__rl\": true, \"mode\": \"list\", \"value\": \"\"} for resource locators. Never invent IDs. Model names: use the one the request names; otherwise the default the catalogue shows for the model field, or leave it empty.",
  "",
  "USEFUL TEMPLATES (n8n core nodes; every other node: use the catalogue):",
  "Set: {\"type\": \"n8n-nodes-base.set\", \"typeVersion\": 3.4, \"parameters\": {\"assignments\": {\"assignments\": [{\"id\": \"a1\", \"name\": \"field\", \"type\": \"string\", \"value\": \"={{ expression }}\"}]}, \"options\": {}}}. It outputs ONLY the fields it sets.",
  "IF (typeVersion 2.2): {\"type\": \"n8n-nodes-base.if\", \"typeVersion\": 2.2, \"parameters\": {\"conditions\": {\"options\": {\"caseSensitive\": true, \"leftValue\": \"\", \"typeValidation\": \"loose\", \"version\": 2}, \"conditions\": [{\"id\": \"c1\", \"leftValue\": \"={{ $('Trigger').item.json.score }}\", \"rightValue\": 2, \"operator\": {\"type\": \"number\", \"operation\": \"lte\"}}], \"combinator\": \"and\"}, \"options\": {}}}. Number operations: equals, notEquals, gt, gte, lt, lte. String: equals, notEquals, contains, startsWith, endsWith. Output 0 = true, output 1 = false. IF/Filter typeVersion 1 uses a different, OLD shape: never mix the two.",
  "Aggregate many items into one list: {\"type\": \"n8n-nodes-base.aggregate\", \"typeVersion\": 1, \"parameters\": {\"fieldsToAggregate\": {\"fieldToAggregate\": [{\"fieldToAggregate\": \"line\"}]}, \"options\": {}}} then read $('<Aggregate name>').item.json.line.join('\\n'). The output field is named after the field you aggregate (here \"line\"): aggregate the field you will read.",
  "Remove records seen in earlier runs: {\"type\": \"n8n-nodes-base.removeDuplicates\", \"typeVersion\": 2, \"parameters\": {\"operation\": \"removeItemsSeenInPreviousExecutions\", \"dedupeValue\": \"={{ $json.id }}\", \"options\": {}}}",
  "Schedule (every hour): {\"type\": \"n8n-nodes-base.scheduleTrigger\", \"typeVersion\": 1.2, \"parameters\": {\"rule\": {\"interval\": [{\"field\": \"hours\", \"hoursInterval\": 1}]}}}. Daily at 08:30: {\"rule\": {\"interval\": [{\"field\": \"days\", \"triggerAtHour\": 8, \"triggerAtMinute\": 30}]}}. Weekdays at 08:30: {\"rule\": {\"interval\": [{\"field\": \"cronExpression\", \"expression\": \"30 8 * * 1-5\"}]}}.",
  "Hacker News top stories: use the Hacker News node with resource \"all\", operation \"getAll\", \"limit\": 10 and \"additionalFields\": {\"tags\": [\"front_page\"]}. It reads Algolia: each story is one item with .objectID (there is no .id), .title, .url, .points and .author. Never use the Firebase API (topstories.json): it returns a bare list of numbers, and n8n cannot turn that into readable items.",
  "Webhook: {\"type\": \"n8n-nodes-base.webhook\", \"typeVersion\": 2, \"parameters\": {\"httpMethod\": \"POST\", \"path\": \"my-path\", \"responseMode\": \"responseNode\", \"options\": {}}} then {\"type\": \"n8n-nodes-base.respondToWebhook\", \"typeVersion\": 1.1, \"parameters\": {\"respondWith\": \"json\", \"responseBody\": \"={{ JSON.stringify({ ok: true }) }}\", \"options\": {}}}. The caller's data: $('Webhook').item.json.body.<field>.",
  "Form trigger: {\"type\": \"n8n-nodes-base.formTrigger\", \"typeVersion\": 2.2, \"parameters\": {\"formTitle\": \"Tell us about you\", \"formFields\": {\"values\": [{\"fieldLabel\": \"Name\", \"requiredField\": true}, {\"fieldLabel\": \"Score\", \"fieldType\": \"dropdown\", \"fieldOptions\": {\"values\": [{\"option\": \"1\"}, {\"option\": \"2\"}]}, \"requiredField\": true}]}, \"options\": {}}}. Each answer: $('Form Trigger').item.json.<field label>.",
  "LLM step: {\"name\": \"Summarise\", \"type\": \"@n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain.chainLlm\", \"typeVersion\": 1.5, \"parameters\": {\"promptType\": \"define\", \"text\": \"={{ 'Summarise: ' + $('Trigger').item.json.text }}\"}} plus a chat model node from the catalogue (its type starts with @n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain.lmChat) connected as \"<model node name>\": {\"ai_languageModel\": [[{\"node\": \"Summarise\", \"type\": \"ai_languageModel\", \"index\": 0}]]}. Reply: $('Summarise').item.json.text.",
  "Route by category: {\"name\": \"Classify\", \"type\": \"@n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain.textClassifier\", \"typeVersion\": 1.1, \"parameters\": {\"inputText\": \"={{ $json.text }}\", \"categories\": {\"categories\": [{\"category\": \"Bug\", \"description\": \"Something is broken\"}, {\"category\": \"Question\", \"description\": \"Asks how to do something\"}]}, \"options\": {}}} plus a chat model node connected with ai_languageModel. Output 0 is the first category, output 1 the second: \"Classify\": {\"main\": [[{\"node\": \"Handle Bug\", \"type\": \"main\", \"index\": 0}], [{\"node\": \"Handle Question\", \"type\": \"main\", \"index\": 0}]]}.",

Fields: $('Extract Details').item.json.output.sender."
].join('\n');

const SEPARATOR = '\n==========\n\n';
const OUTPUT_RULE = '\n\nYou may reason briefly first. Then output the final workflow JSON between <workflow> and </workflow>. Write nothing after </workflow>.';

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Main
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

const state = $json.state;
const spec = state.spec;

const prompt = spec.kind === 'blueprint'
  ? BLUEPRINT_INSTRUCTIONS + SEPARATOR + describeBlueprintTask() + OUTPUT_RULE
  : MONITOR_INSTRUCTIONS + SEPARATOR + describeMonitorTask() + OUTPUT_RULE;

return [{ json: { state, userPrompt: prompt } }];

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Blueprint task
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

function describeBlueprintTask() {
  let task = 'Goal: ' + state.goal + '\n\nSPEC:\n' + JSON.stringify(spec, null, 2);

  // Only values the user wrote in the goal are passed on. Nothing is invented for a blueprint
  // ("#alerts" is a monitor default only).
  if (state.alertEmail && state.goal.includes(state.alertEmail)) {
    task += '\nEmail address to use where email is sent: ' + state.alertEmail;
  }
  if (state.alertSlackChannel && state.goal.includes(state.alertSlackChannel)) {
    task += '\nChannel named in the request (use it exactly): ' + state.alertSlackChannel;
  }
  if (state.userTargetUrl) {
    task += '\nURL mentioned by the user: ' + state.userTargetUrl;
  }

  // Added by Section 7: Node Catalog.
  if ($json.catalogPrompt) {
    task += '\n\nNODES FOR THIS GOAL (exact definitions from the n8n node catalogue: use these types, typeVersions and parameter names exactly; ' +
      'a parameter listed with "when resource=... operation=..." only applies to that resource and operation):\n' + $json.catalogPrompt;
  }

  if (state.previousWorkflow) {
    task += '\n\nWorkflow to repair:\n' + JSON.stringify(withoutNotes(state.previousWorkflow));
  }
  if (state.feedback) {
    task += '\n\nWhat went wrong:\n' + state.feedback + '\n\nFix ONLY the problems listed and return the complete corrected workflow JSON.';
  }
  return task;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Monitor task
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

function describeMonitorTask() {
  const specSummary = { service: spec.service, targetUrl: spec.targetUrl, checks: spec.checks, summary: spec.summary };
  let task = 'Goal: ' + state.goal +
    '\n\nSPEC (implement all of it):\n' + JSON.stringify(specSummary, null, 2) +
    '\n\nProduction targetUrl default (use exactly): ' + spec.targetUrl;

  if (state.userAlertWebhookUrl) {
    task += '\nAlert webhook default (use exactly): ' + state.userAlertWebhookUrl;
  }

  // Slack wins over email when the user gave both.
  if (state.alertSlackChannel) {
    task += describeSlackAlert();
  } else if (state.alertEmail) {
    task += describeEmailAlert();
  }

  return task + describeRepair();
}

// spec.service is placed inside single-quoted expressions below. That is safe because
// "Validate Spec" refuses quotes, backslashes, backticks and $ in a monitor's service name.

function describeSlackAlert() {
  const slackNode = {
    name: 'Send Alert',
    type: 'n8n-nodes-base.slack',
    typeVersion: 2.3,
    position: [0, 0],
    onError: 'continueRegularOutput',
    parameters: {
      resource: 'message',
      operation: 'post',
      select: 'channel',
      channelId: { __rl: true, value: state.alertSlackChannel, mode: 'name' },
      messageType: 'text',
      text: "={{ ':rotating_light: " + spec.service + " is unhealthy: ' + $('Unhealthy').item.json.cause + ' (' + $('Config').item.json.targetUrl + ')' }}",
      otherOptions: {},
    },
  };
  return '\n\nALERT CHANNEL: SLACK channel ' + state.alertSlackChannel + '. The node "Send Alert" is a Slack node instead of the webhook POST:\n' +
    JSON.stringify(slackNode) +
    '\nUse it as shown (you may improve the text). ' + ALERT_NODE_RULES('Slack');
}

function describeEmailAlert() {
  const gmailNode = {
    name: 'Send Alert',
    type: 'n8n-nodes-base.gmail',
    typeVersion: 2.1,
    position: [0, 0],
    onError: 'continueRegularOutput',
    parameters: {
      sendTo: state.alertEmail,
      subject: "={{ '" + spec.service + " is unhealthy: ' + $('Unhealthy').item.json.cause }}",
      emailType: 'text',
      message: "={{ '" + spec.service + " failed its health check.\\n\\nCause: ' + $('Unhealthy').item.json.cause + '\\nEndpoint: ' + $('Config').item.json.targetUrl }}",
      options: { appendAttribution: false },
    },
  };
  return '\n\nALERT CHANNEL: EMAIL to ' + state.alertEmail + '. The node "Send Alert" is a Gmail node instead of the webhook POST:\n' +
    JSON.stringify(gmailNode) +
    '\nUse it as shown (you may improve subject and message). ' + ALERT_NODE_RULES('Gmail');
}

// The same closing rules for the Slack and the Gmail alert node.
function ALERT_NODE_RULES(accountName) {
  return 'Do NOT add credentials: the user connects ' + accountName + ' after creation. ' +
    'Keep the Config field alertWebhookUrl unchanged. "Result Alert" still appends \' (alert delivery failed)\' when $json.error is set.';
}

// Repair part of the monitor prompt.
// The model repairs its BEST tested draft, not simply the last one, so a worse attempt is never built on.
function describeRepair() {
  const best = state.best;
  const workflowToRepair = best?.workflow || state.previousWorkflow;
  const feedbackToFix = best?.workflow ? best.feedback : state.feedback;
  let repair = '';

  if (state.regressed) {
    repair += '\n\nYour last attempt scored ' + state.regressed + ', worse than your best (' + best.score + '). Discard it and start from your best version below.';
  }
  if (workflowToRepair) {
    repair += '\n\nWorkflow to repair:\n' + JSON.stringify(withoutNotes(workflowToRepair));
  }
  if (feedbackToFix) {
    repair += '\n\nWhat went wrong:\n' + feedbackToFix +
      '\n\nFix ONLY the problems listed. Keep every part that already works unchanged. Return the complete corrected workflow JSON.';
  }

  // The last repair of the best draft was rejected before testing (invalid, or refused by the n8n API).
  // Without this, the model gets the same prompt as last time and tends to repeat the same mistake.
  if (best?.workflow && state.feedback && state.feedback !== best.feedback) {
    repair += '\n\nYour last repair of this workflow was rejected for a different reason. Do not repeat it:\n' + state.feedback;
  }
  return repair;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Helpers
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

// A finished draft carries The Alchemist's Setup note ("Fill in", "Double-check"...). If it stays in,
// the model reads it as instructions and copies its words into fields. So the repair prompt only
// gets the real nodes and the connections.
function withoutNotes(workflow) {
  return {
    nodes: (workflow.nodes || []).filter((node) => node && node.type !== 'n8n-nodes-base.stickyNote'),
    connections: workflow.connections,
  };
}

## Section 5: Test (Monitors)
**Draft workflow in, scored results out.**

- Generates rigorous test cases from the spec (e.g., HTTP 500, timeouts, missing fields).
- Runs the draft inline against the internal mock webhook and scores the results.
- Executes a final live smoke-test against the production URL.
- Failures loop back to Build for repair; passes proceed to Deploy.

## Section 6: Deploy
**Workflow in, live n8n workflow out.**

- Pushes the generated draft to your n8n instance via the API.
- API rejections loop back to Build; API credential errors halt execution immediately.
- Auto-activates monitors with valid alert webhooks. Blueprints are left inactive for safety.
- Outputs the final chat verdict, workflow link, and setup instructions.

## Section 4: Review (Blueprints)
**Validated draft in, finished blueprint out.**

- A second LLM reviews the logic against the user's original intent and n8n's verified schema facts.
- Merges validator warnings and review defects to write the user's Setup note.
- Findings trigger up to two targeted repair rounds in the Build loop.
- Always delivers the best valid draft, even if some review warnings remain.

nodes.name: Fetch Output Schemas
nodes.notes: Downloads n8n's own sample output schemas for the draft's nodes (most tried versions do not exist: those errors are expected and skipped).

parameters.content:
## Main lane
**Chat message in, chat reply out.**

- Chat Trigger > Settings > Read Request: reads the goal, URLs, alert target and daily limits.
- Check Mock Webhook tests that the built-in mock (Section 8) answers. Initialize Case checks the request and creates the state.
- The loop: Case Finished? > Run Section > Decide Next Step. Run Section calls this workflow for the next section, and Decide Next Step picks what comes next: the next section, a repair round, or a reply.
- Format Chat Reply > Send Reply: turns the result into chat text and remembers an open question for the same chat.

## Section 8: Test Mock
**Config in, simulated HTTP response out.**

- Built-in webhook acting as a local test bench for monitor validation.
- Simulates any status code, response body, content type, or network delay (up to 30s).
- Required by Section 5 (Test) to verify monitor accuracy before deployment. Must be active before use.

## Section 7: Node Catalog
**Catalog in, node definitions out.**

- Fetches pinned core and AI node catalogs from jsdelivr based on current version settings.
- Filters and delivers exact parameter definitions, versions, and credentials for the Build phase.
- Locates and downloads n8n's internal sample output schemas for the Check and Review phases.

## Section 3: Check
**Draft in, verified plan or errors out.**

- Validates blueprint drafts against n8n's actual node catalog, parameter requirements, and expression syntax.
- Blocks unauthorized system-access nodes and malformed connection arrays.
- Generates precise warnings and syntax errors to feed back into the Build repair loop.
